HEADLINE: the live fusion screen's available combos are serialized as raw component pairs (h1/h2 = HeroType enums, idx1/idx2 = slot indices) plus an AI score and a bad-combo flag. There is NO result name field and NO result effect-text field. GetComboScore/IsBadCombo judge a pair but the game never hands the bridge a composed fused description.

writer.WriteString("name_loc", Loc(info.GetNameSlug()));
writer.WriteString("desc_loc", Loc(info.GetDescSlug()));

claims.detail: Name and description are read as per-entity I2 term slugs (GetNameSlug / GetDescSlug). Plugin.cs never builds an "A X B" string — it always looks up a single entity's translation. The fused name format therefore lives in game code, not in any data asset the dump captured.

text: var typeName = I2.Loc.LocalizationManager.GetTranslation(term, true, 0, true, false, null, null, true);

claims.detail: Loc() is a pure term lookup in the I2Languages table — no string formatting, no pair substitution. Reinforces that any "{0} X {1}" style template would have to be applied by the game's own name-building code before display, and is not visible through this bridge.

STRONG STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE: a fused ball in the live save is one ball instance (type + lvl) carrying a `combined` list of absorbed HeroTypes — not a new entity with its own name/desc. The game models a fusion as base + absorbed components and must assemble the display text from those parts. This is the closest thing to a composition model found in game-derived code.

claims.detail: desc_fill.py: "The game file's (I2Loc) description is only the template; the game fills in the values at runtime." This is the ONLY text-generation mechanism found in any game-derived code — and it fills {[stat]} placeholders inside ONE ball's template from PropertiesByLvl. It does not merge two balls' effect texts. There is no fusion-text composer in this ecosystem.

const shouldSwap = left.en > right.en;

claims.detail: ballbylon canonicalizes the name by sorting component names alphabetically (shouldSwap = left.en > right.en). This is a FAN convention for a stable id — the wiki says the game uses acquisition order instead, so the real in-game name follows which ball was picked up first. Do not treat alphabetical order as the game's naming rule.

claims.detail: Fan-generated summary: "Fusion result: retains the effects of BOTH X and Y." Closest thing to a fused-effect-text rule found outside the wiki — but it is a fixed fan sentence, not a game template. The actual in-game tooltip appears to be built by stacking the two components' ability texts rather than by filling a format string.

text: 两个自毁型球融合时，可能丢失其中一个爆炸/自毁效果。

claims.detail: ballbylon warns: "When two self-destruct balls are fused, one of their explosion/self-destruct effects may be lost." Matches the wiki's Destroy caveat. A fan heuristic (both tags include "destroy" → −12 score), but it encodes a real cross-component interaction the naive "just concatenate both texts" model would miss.

text: Fused Balls will have the name and effects of their fused balls combined, and their icon will also be updated to match the fusion. For example, fusing '''Bleed''' and '''Freeze''' will result in '''Bleed X Freeze''', which has both abilities from '''Bleed''' and '''Freeze'''.

claims.detail: THE GENERATIVE RULE (prose, not a format string): fused name = "A X B"; fused effects = BOTH components' abilities. No template string is given. This is the closest public statement to "how fused effect text is composed" — a union of the two components' abilities, not a templated sentence with placeholders.

text: The priority of which effects and stats are combined are dependent on the component balls involved.

claims.detail: THE OPEN PROBLEM: stat/effect merge priority is component-dependent and undocumented. This is why fused damage/proc/cooldown numbers cannot be derived from public sources. Ability *structure* can be composed; numbers cannot.

text: the order of the fused balls does not change the functional stats/abilities of the resulting ball, its name will be different and its appearance ''may'' be different depending on the specific balls fused

claims.detail: Order affects name and sprite only; function is order-independent. Contradicts any source claiming order changes behavior. Name order follows acquisition order ("the only way to change the order of fused balls is to change the order in which they're acquired"), not alphabetical sort.

text: Spawn is arguably the best ability. It can compensate Destroy effect. For example, Cell(Clone) x Bomb(Destroy) is an "indestructible" bomb, since the bomb is cloned and destroyed at the same time.

claims.detail: Documented cross-component interaction: one component's Spawn compensates the other's Destroy. Proves fused behavior is more than naive text concatenation — the components' trigger types interact. Cross-links the wiki's ability-type model with real fusion outcomes.

text: Destroy: Balls destroy after hit. Though regarded as the least‑favoured type, these balls are usually having powerful abilities. Note: fusing two Destroy balls may lose one of their abililies.

claims.detail: Two Destroy balls may lose one ability. (Source typo "abililies" is verbatim.) Corroborated independently by ballbylon-helper's destroy-pair warning. Suggests the composition rule is not a pure union — some same-trigger pairs drop a component.
